subject: Tenant output licensing, onshore processing and subprocessor proof requests
content:
From: Alyssa Morgan <alyssa.morgan@healthscale.com>
To: rohan_mehta@redwood.ai
Cc: procure@healthscale.com
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Tenant licensing & processing proof — quick asks

Hi Rohan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we move toward an SOW and DPA, legal/procurement have two quick gating asks we need answered before we route to exec sign-off: 

1) Tenant output licensing: Can Redwood confirm that customer-generated prompts and model outputs are "tenant-owned" and not used for model improvement by default unless we opt in via a documented mechanism? We need the language in the DPA or an addendum.

2) Onshore processing & subprocessors: For PHI-adjacent workloads we require either onshore processing or an onshore-only subprocessor list with evidence. Please provide current subprocessor inventory and any proof you can share (SOC2 attestations, contracts, or statements of residency).

3) Evidence package: If you can attach a short package (inventory CSV + any attestations), we can evaluate and get procurement to circulate a limited redline.

I’m attaching our expected DPA template with a few redlines. If these are straightforward, we can aim for a week turnaround.

Best,
Alyssa
Head of Procurement, HealthScale

Attachment: HealthScale_DPA_Redlines.pdf

-----Original Message-----

From: rohan_mehta@redwood.ai
To: Alyssa Morgan <alyssa.morgan@healthscale.com>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenant licensing & processing proof — quick asks

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Dev (security/ops) and Karthik (privacy/legal) to help collate evidence.

Short answers up front:
- Tenant output licensing: Redwood supports an opt-out of model improvement (no-training) at the tenant level. By default, we do not surface customer prompts/outputs to public model training without explicit opt-in or contractual carveouts — but we do collect telemetry for service operation. Karthik/Legal will confirm precise DPA language.
- Onshore processing: We operate multi-region clusters; for HealthScale workloads we can route inference to US-only hosts and restrict cross-border backups per a Residency SLO in the Dedicated/Private offering.

Action items:
- Dev to attach current subprocessor inventory + SOC2 link and a short note describing residency controls.
- Karthik to propose DPA clause wording for "tenant output licensing" and a no-train toggle.

I’ll follow up with a consolidated evidence package by EOD Thu.

—Rohan
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Thanks Rohan — procurement wanted to confirm the format of proof. A CSV with subprocessors + country is fine, but we also need a short statement describing the isolation model for tenant data (how you ensure a tenant’s prompts/outputs aren’t mixed into improvement workflows). A one-page ops note is ideal.

Also, can you confirm whether onshore routing is included in Dedicated by default or if that’s a paid add-on? We’re evaluating cost.

Alyssa

-----Original Message-----

From: dev_patel@redwood.ai
To: Alyssa Morgan <alyssa.morgan@healthscale.com>
Cc: rohan_mehta@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 13:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenant licensing & processing proof — quick asks

Hi Alyssa — attaching the requested artifacts. See inline answers below.

Attachments: subprocessor_inventory_2026-10.csv; redis-soc2-link.txt; tenant-isolation-ops-1pager.txt

1) Subprocessor inventory: attached CSV lists each subprocessor, service (hosting, monitoring, log retention), and processing country. The top-level compute/data-plane for Hosted/ Dedicated runs in the provider region you choose (we have US-east / US-west / eu-west clusters).

2) Tenant isolation & no-train: By default, tenant prompts/responses are not included in model training pipelines. We expose a per-tenant "Improvement Opt-in" flag in our control plane; customers using Hosted may need an enterprise feature flag. For Private deployments, the flag is controlled by tenant admins. Operationally: we maintain a separate ingestion queue with a tagging layer; data marked as "do-not-learn" is filtered before any model improvement job. The one-pager (attached) sketches the ingestion filter, KV cache isolation, and retention windowing.

3) Onshore routing & pricing: Onshore-only routing is available on Dedicated and Private. For Dedicated it is included in the baseline SLA if you commit to a reserved capacity block >= 2 GPUs per model endpoint; otherwise it’s a small per-region routing premium. I’ll have our account team provide a cost delta estimate.

Let me know if the CSV and one-pager are sufficient for procurement. Happy to hop on a short call if you want walk-through.

—Dev
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — received the CSV and the one-pager. Quick follow-ups: 

- The one-pager is helpful. Legal asked for the exact DPA sentence we could insert that commits to "no model training" on tenant data unless explicitly opted in. Can Karthik provide proposed text we can use directly?
- Procurement would like an exportable proof-of-residency statement (a brief signed letter or a statement of where backups persist). Is that something Redwood can provide for the SOW?
- Can you also confirm whether logs (debug/tracing) are captured with full prompts by default and whether those logs are covered by the same no-train commitment?

If you can drop the proposed DPA language and the residency statement by EOD Monday we’ll circulate to legal. Thanks for the quick turnaround.

Best,
Alyssa
Head of Procurement, HealthScale
